exposure: intraoperative ventilation parameters (tidal volume, expired minute ventilation, positive end-expiratory pressure, mean airway pressure, peak inspiratory pressure, compliance, plateau pressure)
cohort: 680 adult patients with moderate to severe COPD admitted to the ICU from the operating room following elective non-cardiac surgery.
finding: Most intraoperative ventilation parameters had no significant association with mortality, postoperative mechanical ventilation, or vasopressor use, although tidal volume correlated positively with some postoperative white blood cell counts, and plateau pressure showed a strong positive association with the neutrophil-to-lymphocyte ratio.
